dimensions.assessment: Directly affects federally qualified health centers, health care providers, and patients served by these centers, particularly those with high rates of diet-related chronic disease or food insecurity.
dimensions.evidence: prioritize health centers serving populations with high rates of diet-related chronic disease, food insecurity, or other nutrition-related health disparities

dimensions.assessment: Introduces patient-centered nutrition education, dietary counseling, and interdisciplinary care models into primary care delivery and workforce training.
dimensions.evidence: patient-centered nutrition education and counseling services

dimensions.assessment: Authorizes the use of existing funding made available under section 10503(a)(1) of the Patient Protection and Affordable Care Act to award grants, contracts, or cooperative agreements.
dimensions.evidence: utilize existing funding, made available under section 10503(a)(1) of the Patient Protection and Affordable Care Act

dimensions.assessment: Amends the Public Health Service Act to add a specific nutrition education and chronic disease prevention initiative to section 330.
dimensions.evidence: To amend the Public Health Service Act to authorize funding for nutrition education and chronic disease prevention at federally qualified health centers

dimensions.assessment: Requires annual reports to Congress through fiscal year 2031, establishing an ongoing multi-year reporting and evaluation mechanism.

missing_information: Exact monetary amounts for grants or contracts are not specified in the text.
importance_detail.rationale: H.R. 9389 authorizes funding and a grant initiative for integrating nutrition education and chronic disease prevention into primary care delivery at federally qualified health centers, prioritizing populations with high rates of diet-related health disparities.
